fixes.row: There is no one who does not sin; all have sinned; if we say we have not sinned
fixes.why: 1 John 2:1 says “so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate”. It names no universal sinning and does not match the row's quoted words. Wesleyan readers take it as the apostle's aim for believers, and Catholic readers hear the advocate and the sacrament of reconciliation in it; placed here it reads as a verse on universal sin. It is already in the commands row, where it fits.
fixes.fix: Remove 1John.2.1 from this row (it stays in “Do not sin”, row 19).

fixes.row: If someone sins: the Law's cases, sinning unintentionally; sinning deliberately
fixes.why: Hebrews 10:26 is not a Law case. The heading “the Law's cases” sets it beside Num 15:30 as though the text ruled on deliberate sin under the Law. Reformed and Baptist readers take this verse as the perseverance question, and the row's heading makes a verdict out of a question the page says it leaves open.
fixes.fix: Relabel to “If someone sins: the Law's cases, unintentionally; sinning defiantly or deliberately (Num 15:30; Heb 10:26)”, so the heading names the two kinds of sin and does not claim the Law's cases cover both. Keep the row count; the note already says readers part on Heb 10:26.

fixes.why: The note quotes “bear their sin; they shall die childless” as the text's words for Num 18:22. The Berean prints “they will incur guilt and die” (checked on localhost:8012), and no Berean verse says “childless”. A reader who opens the verse finds different English from the note, and the rabbi reading the Hebrew hears a rendering the page supplied.
fixes.fix: Quote the Berean: “they will incur guilt and die”. If the Hebrew sense is to be given, mark it as the page's own rendering of the Hebrew, not as the text's words.

fixes.row: The sins of the kings: “the sin Jeroboam caused Israel to commit”, Baasha, Manasseh
readers: all seats (rule 7: the row count is 26, above 25)
fixes.why: Rule 7 asks to flag rows that say the same thing. The verb row “He caused Israel to sin” (row 24) says what the noun row (row 16) says in the same Hebrew causative: the same kings, the same causing, the same verses in the same books. Together they are 26 rows, one more than the reader's range.
fixes.fix: Merge row 24 into row 16, or justify keeping both in the worker's report. If the forms must stay apart, say in row 24's note that it is the verb of row 16's phrase.

worker_points.point: Rom 8:3 under the sin offering (row 14), the Greek being “concerning sin”
worker_points.why: The Berean says “as an offering for sin”, and the note says the Greek is “concerning sin”. The note is candid, and the row is a fair place for it.

worker_points.why: Christ is named in 2 Cor 5:19-20 in the same passage, and the note says the sentence names him. The row's heading does not depend on the pronoun.

examples_checked: 23 of 26 rows: all four examples show their label. Rows 10 (Rev 18:5 under “bear the consequences”), 15 (Matt 1:21 under a label of other phrases) and 17 (1 John 2:1 under “if we say we have not sinned”) each have one example that does not; row 23's Heb 10:26 shows only its “deliberately” clause.
summary: The hub is accurate to the Berean in nearly every row, and the three-way side-by-side treatment of the contested points takes no side. Four fixes are needed: one misplaced verse (1 John 2:1), one misfiled verse under the Law's cases (Heb 10:26), one note that quotes a rendering the Berean does not give (Num 18:22), and one duplicated row (rows 16 and 24) that takes the count to 26.
